items.title: Tony Marino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 25, 2025
items.q: the first gig I ever played in New York City was with him at Fat Tuesday’s

ctx.x: This will be totally speculative, but you’ve played with some marvelous saxophone players over the years and I’m thinking in my mind comparing like Zoot Sims with Dave Liebman. Zoot Sims probably came early in your career.

Yeah. Well I used to – being here in Pennsylvania, Phil Woods’ band was in town you know, and Phil lived in Delaware Water Gap. And his rhythm section guys lived in the Poconos. So I was associated with them. And it’s word of mouth musicians you know. And also in our area I’ll say, Al Cohn – Al Cohn I was at a restaurant playing somewhere and he liked me. So that was the first gig I ever played in New York City was with him at Fat Tuesday’s, a club called Fat Tuesday’s, and we played downstairs. And so that…
tunes, not learning enough tunes. So that was basically part of our discussion while he hit a little vodka on the side there.
